identity_evidence.quote: A right-handed, 25-year-old male, a fire alarm repair technician

attribution_limitations: The phrase "since 3 months after a trivial, blunt trauma" does not settle whether 3 months is how long the inability has lasted or the interval from trauma to onset; the discussion calls the patient "3 months post-rupture" without stating the rupture date.

The right side is stated for the finger-extension loss; the fracture is placed "in the same limb", and the Figure 2 and 4 captions label the nail radiographs as the right hand and distal forearm. The tendon rupture, ultrasonography and operative sentences do not state a side.
The proximal and distal cut-end positions follow the ultrasonography sentence but the sentence does not name the method; the two proximal values are not assigned to a specific tendon.

The discussion says a different technique (cut distal end of EIP adjacent to EDC) "could have been performed" and that FDS transfer would have delayed rehabilitation; these are counterfactual alternatives, not procedures done.

claims.text: A right-handed 25-year-old male fire alarm repair technician presented with inability to extend his right index finger since 3 months after a trivial, blunt trauma to the dorsum of his distal forearm. He had sustained a distal radius fracture in the same limb 2.5 years ago due to an accidental fall, fixed with an intramedullary titanium elastic nail system (TENS), after which he regained full wrist and finger motion.

claims.text: Examination showed complete loss of active extension of the right index finger at the MCP joint, with extension of the other fingers and the thumb preserved. Ultrasonography showed complete discontinuity of both EDC and EIP tendons of the index finger with a 6-cm gap, and radiographs showed the TENS nail in the radius with its dorsal tip abutting the extensor compartment. The authors state the cause was chronic attrition against newly formed bone around the retained nail.

claims.text: Under regional anesthesia a Z incision was made on the dorsal wrist and distal forearm, and the extensor retinaculum was partially opened. Both tendons were ruptured with frayed cut ends about 6 cm apart and the EPL intact. New bone at the nail entry point was removed by burring, the nail could not be removed, its protruding end was cut short and the remainder left in place. The EDC was reconstructed with a palmaris longus graft; the very thin EIP was not reconstructed.
